euronews.description: The “no war, no peace” US-Iran confrontation appears to be moving towards a possible breaking point as Iran increases its military actions in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, while its critical attempt to break the US military naval blockade in the Persian Gulf appears to be imminent.

euronews.description: Mexican special forces captured drug kingpin Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “Chapo Isidro”, during a raid in Sinaloa, with footage showing soldiers escorting him into an army vehicle.

euronews.title: Thousands take to streets in Portugal, France and Spain over rising living costs
euronews.description: Thousands of people demonstrated in Portugal and France on Saturday, calling for higher wages, affordable housing and action to tackle the rising cost of living. In Lisbon, workers marched despite heavy rain, while trade unions, Yellow Vest activists and youth groups gathered in Paris.

euronews.title: Paolo Bulgari, Italian jewellery tycoon, dies aged 89
euronews.description: The grandson of Bulgari's founder helped transform the family jewellery business into one of the world's most prestigious luxury brands. He led the Roman maison as chairman from 1984 and remained passionate about jewellery design throughout his life.

euronews.title: New documentary: Princess Kate speaks candidly about how cancer changed her body and mind
euronews.description: The Princess of Wales opens up about the physical and emotional impact of her cancer diagnosis in a deeply personal BBC documentary. Kate also reflects on her recovery, finding hope amid uncertainty and learning to live with a new perspective on life.

euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 21st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: Real Madrid outpace Bayern Munich in revenue race as both clubs post record figures
euronews.description: Real Madrid have widened the financial gap over Bayern Munich, generating more than €1.2 billion in revenue in the 2025-26 season. The German champions are also approaching the billion-euro mark, while celebrating a record 500,000 members.

euronews.title: Estonia-Russia border closure sends residents rushing to cross before deadline
euronews.description: Families and travellers are queuing to cross from Russia into Estonia before all five road border crossings are shut on 1 December. The decision follows an alleged Russian-backed sabotage attempt, but has also raised concerns among people with relatives on both sides of the border.

euronews.title: Former Costa Concordia cruise ship captain released from prison on probation after nine years
euronews.description: The case dates back to January 2012, when the Costa Concordia ship struck rocks off the coast of Isola del Giglio in the Tyrrhenian Sea. The disaster claimed 32 lives.

euronews.title: Raccoon roast as a sustainable alternative to Germany's Christmas goose?
euronews.description: A chef from Thuringia serves the furry pest with red cabbage and dumplings, praising its tender meat. Could it become the new Christmas favourite?

euronews.title: Brazil ex-president Bolsonaro in intensive care over intestinal problem
euronews.description: The former Brazilian president was taken to hospital with abdominal pain, accompanied by military police.

euronews.title: Mexico captures FBI’s most-wanted cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’, triggering violence
euronews.description: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, one of the FBI’s ten most-wanted fugitives, was arrested in a military operation involving US intelligence cooperation. Gunfire, burning vehicles and panic among civilians followed the raid in northern Mexico. 11 people were killed.

euronews.title: Russian cargo ship struck by drones in Gulf of Finland
euronews.description: The United States announced sanctions against the Sparta II in early May 2022, just over two months after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Ukraine has also sanctioned the vessel.

euronews.title: Ballistic missile attack on Zelenskyy's hometown kills two people
euronews.description: The strike mainly targeted civilian infrastructure, Zelenskyy wrote on X. The attack comes after Russia vowed a 'painful' response to Ukraine's strike on the Crimean bridge.

euronews.title: EU budget: Costa pitches more cuts, Big Tech tax to break deadlock
euronews.description: European Council President António Costa proposes cutting the EU's 2028-2034 budget by nearly €200bn, a 10% reduction, to win over frugal countries. Cohesion funding is cut for the first time. A 3% digital services levy replaces a controversial corporate tax, and debt repayment is slowed down.

euronews.title: Strait of Hormuz: Athlete swims through war zone to expose war's environmental toll
euronews.description: British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh completed a 15-kilometre swim through the Strait of Hormuz over three days in November 2026, braving explosions and burning tankers nearby. His three-day challenge aimed to expose the environmental damage caused by the war with Iran.

euronews.title: European Union and Indonesia sign free trade deal after decade of talks
euronews.description: Trade between the EU and Indonesia was valued at €28.9 billion in 2025, with EU exports worth €10.2 billion and EU imports worth €18.7 billion.

euronews.title: Hagia Sophia's hidden tunnels uncovered as 420 metres of underground network cleaned
euronews.description: During cleaning and excavation works carried out at the site, significant remains were uncovered and carefully documented by archaeologists.

lemonde.title: Fuites de Beauvau vers le RN : d’un email trouvé au domicile d’un ami de Marine Le Pen aux suspicions visant le préfet Hugues Moutouh, itinéraire d’une enquête sensible
lemonde.description: Le préfet a demandé sa mise en retrait après la révélation de suspicions le visant dans l’enquête sur les fuites d’informations confidentielles vers le RN. D’après les informations du « Monde », les investigations ont été déclenchées après la découverte d’un courriel d’une fonctionnaire de Beauvau au domicile à Rome de Frédéric Chatillon, un proche de Marine Le Pen.

lemonde.title: « Nous sommes face à de nouvelles socialisations politiques » : les mobilisations en France, en Italie et en Allemagne vues par les philosophes Michaël Fœssel et Martin Rueff
lemonde.description: Le spécialiste de la philosophie allemande et le connaisseur de la pensée italienne reviennent, dans un entretien au « Monde », sur l’articulation entre les dimensions politique, sociale et générationnelle des mouvements qui secouent les trois pays depuis septembre.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : François Ruffin renonce à sa candidature « face au risque » de l’arrivée de l’extrême droite au pouvoir
lemonde.description: Le député de la Somme n’apporte son soutien à aucun candidat et souhaite « bon courage et bonne campagne » aux « candidats de gauche encore en lice », sans les citer, « pour porter un projet à vocation majoritaire » face à un Rassemblement national « aux portes du pouvoir ».

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, France-Argentine : Kalvin Gourgues creuse l’écart pour les Bleus, en route vers la finale du Championnat des nations
lemonde.description: Le XV de France dispute, samedi au Stade de France, son dernier match de la phase de groupes du Championnat des nations, face aux Pumas argentins. S’ils conservent la tête de la poule Nord, les Bleus joueront la première finale de la compétition.

lemonde.title: Les mystères de Mercure, l’étrange planète du Système solaire, que la mission BepiColombo devrait lever
lemonde.description: Après huit ans de transit, les deux sondes de la mission européano-japonaise se sont mises en orbite autour de Mercure. Elles devraient aider les scientifiques à résoudre les nombreuses énigmes qui entourent cette petite planète pas comme les autres.

lemonde.title: Faire l’amour en se faisant la guerre : comment les adeptes du « hate sex » lient colère et coït
lemonde.description: « Nos émotions : la colère ». Une sexualité épanouie, synonyme de complicité avec son ou sa partenaire, semble a priori incompatible avec la colère, qui rend agressif et égoïste. Et pourtant… livres et films témoignent qu’il existe bel et bien des amateurs de « sexe enragé ».

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : le point sur l’attaque par drone d’un cargo russe en mer Baltique, la Finlande soupçonne un hélicoptère russe d’avoir violé son espace aérien
lemonde.description: « Cette violation présumée de l’espace aérien pourrait être liée à des opérations de sauvetage ou de surveillance menées à la suite des dommages subis par un navire cargo dans le golfe de Finlande », a déclaré le ministre de la défense finlandais, Antti Häkkänen.

lemonde.title: Israël : Gadi Eisenkot invite le parti de Benyamin Nétanyahou à des négociations de coalition
lemonde.description: M. Eisenkot a jusqu’au mois prochain pour former un gouvernement, à la suite des législatives de la fin d’octobre, qui n’ont dégagé aucune majorité absolue, ni pour son camp ni pour celui du premier ministre sortant.

lemonde.title: Roberto Saviano, auteur de « Gomorra » : « Le suicide de l’ancien chef de la police italienne Gianni De Gennaro est un choc immense »
lemonde.description: Ce suicide, le 21 novembre, intervient quelques jours après sa mise en examen pour « détournement d’enquête » par le parquet de Caltanissetta, en Sicile, qui l’accuse d’avoir brouillé les pistes dans les investigations sur l’assassinat du juge antimafia Paolo Borsellino, le 19 juillet 1992. Pour l’écrivain italien, cela « pourrait condamner tout espoir de connaître un jour l’entière vérité » sur cette affaire mais aussi sur le meurtre d’un autre juge antimafia, Giovanni Falcone.

lemonde.title: A Genève, la communauté internationale échoue à interdire les robots tueurs
lemonde.description: Alors que la menace des systèmes d’armes létales autonomes, désormais assistées par l’intelligence artificielle, se fait chaque jour plus précise dans les zones de combat, la Russie, les Etats-Unis et Israël se sont opposés à l’ouverture de négociations pour un traité international sur ce type d’armes.

lemonde.title: Quand Ninho et Koba LaD dévoilent les dessous du rap dans deux « documentaires-vérité »
lemonde.description: Deux films, diffusés sur Netflix et Prime Video, promettent de tout révéler sur le parcours des deux artistes, des arnaques jusqu’aux démêlés judiciaires. Décryptage de deux formules à succès.

lemonde.title: Bahreïn accuse l’Iran d’avoir frappé l’un de ses sites industriels
lemonde.description: Plus tôt samedi, l’Iran avait affirmé avoir intercepté un drone américain visant l’île de Qeshm, dans le détroit d’Ormuz. Les gardiens de la révolution ont dit avoir visé à plusieurs reprises cette semaine des installations américaines à Bahreïn.

lemonde.title: Génocide des Rohingya : la Cour internationale de justice rend un arrêt pour l’histoire
lemonde.description: La plus haute Cour de l’ONU établit pour la première fois la responsabilité d’un Etat, la Birmanie, dans « le crime des crimes ». Alors que l’Afrique du Sud a saisi l’institution contre Israël, accusant l’Etat hébreu d’un génocide contre les Palestiniens de Gaza, l’arrêt prononcé jeudi pourrait faire jurisprudence.

lemonde.title: Avec le lyrique « L’Enclos des esclaves », la romancière Najwa Bin Shatwan ravive Benghazi, en Libye, au tournant du XXᵉ siècle
lemonde.description: Ce beau roman de l’écrivaine libyenne revient sur la question douloureuse de l’esclavage en Libye aux XIXᵉ et XXᵉsiècle, en suivant une fille d’esclave en quête de ses origines.

lemonde.title: « The Greatest », sur Prime Video : de Cassius Clay à Muhammad Ali, des Jeux olympiques de Rome au championnat du monde des poids lourds à Miami
lemonde.description: La fiction créée par Ben Watkins retrace avec rigueur l’ascension du jeune boxeur devenu porte-parole de sa communauté.

lemonde.title: En Ligue 1, des entraîneurs plus interchangeables que jamais
lemonde.description: Alors que l’été avait déjà été riche en remaniements sur les bancs du championnat de France, quatre clubs reprennent, après la trêve internationale, avec un nouvel entraîneur. Des changements à Lens, Strasbourg, Le Havre et Lyon, symboles d’une grande instabilité.

rfi.title: EU proposes digital tax to fund budget as France and Germany clash over cuts
rfi.description: The European Union has unveiled plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to help finance its next long-term budget, as Brussels seeks to overcome deep divisions between member states over spending priorities. The proposal has already drawn criticism from France and Germany, highlighting the challenge of securing an agreement before the end of the year.

rfi.title: Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France
rfi.description: Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.

rfi.title: National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms
rfi.description: France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.

rfi.title: French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer
rfi.description: A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.

rfi.title: Former PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid with warning to far right
rfi.description: Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election, promising to restore France's international influence, tackle growing inequality and challenge the rise of the far right. The veteran conservative also delivered a blistering assessment of President Emmanuel Macron's leadership, accusing him of allowing the country's political and social divisions to deepen.

rfi.title: France must change or 'risk losing' overseas territories, former PM tells RFI
rfi.description: France's territories outside Europe are a major strategic asset, giving it a foothold on five continents and in three oceans. Yet Paris has long been accused of neglecting the nearly 3 million people living outside mainland France, who face deep economic and social inequalities. With calls for independence growing, former prime minister Manuel Valls warns that France risks losing its overseas territories unless it radically changes its relationship with them.

rfi.title: Cost of living protests set to continue across Europe over weekend
rfi.description: Protests across Europe against conditions in schools, housing and the soaring cost of living are set to continue throughout the weekend, with hundreds of thousands expected to take to the streets in countries across the continent – including France, Belgium, Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom.

rfi.title: UN climate talks run into overtime as countries clash over fossil fuel cuts
rfi.description: Deep divisions over fossil fuels and financial support for poorer nations pushed the Cop31 climate summit in Turkey beyond its scheduled closing day on Friday, as nearly 200 countries struggled to agree on how to tackle global warming.

rfi.title: Turkey seizes control of last major independent news channel amid fraud scandal
rfi.description: Turkey's last operating independent TV news channel has fallen under state control, as President Recep Tayyip Erdogan scrambles to contain a wave of public fury over a $20 billion investment fund scandal that has swallowed the life savings of hundreds of thousands of people in the country.

rfi.title: French Greens candidate gives hard-left Mélenchon a boost in presidential race
rfi.description: French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has said an alliance with the Greens "should be possible", after the head of the Greens tentatively agreed to back him, angering moderates on the centre-left.

rfi.title: France probes suspected leaks from interior ministry to far-right National Rally
rfi.description: France has opened a probe into suspicions that a senior official at the interior ministry leaked secret information to the far-right National Rally (RN) party, which is itself facing a number of investigations, prosecutors have said.

rfi.title: Depardieu and Houellebecq accused of gang rape on French film set
rfi.description: Paris prosecutors have opened an investigation after an actress filed a complaint alleging that she was raped by a group including actor Gérard Depardieu and high-profile French author Michel Houellebecq on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018.

rfi.title: EU and UK agree 'landmark' deal at Burnham's Brussels summit
rfi.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU's top officials on Friday sealed deals to ease trade and youth mobility at a summit in Brussels, billed as a first step in a push to rebuild ties after Brexit.

rfi.title: Nigeria moves to end prison sentences for attempted suicide
rfi.description: President Bola Tinubu has asked the Nigerian parliament to decriminalise attempted ​suicide and provide support for people who have tried to take their own lives. The move is aimed at ​treating ‌suicide attempts as a ⁠mental health issue rather than a criminal offence, in a country where access to psychological healthcare is limited and suicidal thoughts are often treated as a spiritual affliction.

rfi.title: Africa accounts for half of world's children living in conflict zones, NGO warns
rfi.description: Around 260 million children in Africa were living close to armed conflict in 2025 – amounting to two in five, a larger proportion than ever previously recorded, the charity Save the Children said in a report on Thursday. Worldwide, nearly one in four children lived near fighting.

rfi.title: Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya, says top UN court
rfi.description: Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, the International Court of Justice said on Thursday in an historic ruling, ordering refugees be given safe passage home and awarded compensation.

rfi.title: EU delays new methane emissions rules until 2029 despite climate concerns
rfi.description: The European Union has agreed to postpone new methane emissions regulations for two years, giving the oil and gas industry more time to adapt amid mounting pressure on global energy markets. But environmental groups warn the decision risks undermining climate ambitions.

rfi.title: Europe left out in the cold as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
rfi.description: As the leaders of the United States, China and Russia held historic talks in the Chinese city of Shenzhen on Thursday, representatives of the European Union – the world's largest trading bloc – were conspicuously absent, despite the fact the discussions could have far-reaching consequences for Europe.

zeit.description: Borussia Dortmund hat die Tabellenführung übernommen, Freiburg ist jetzt punktgleich mit den Bayern. In Frankfurt wurden zwei Elfmeter verschossen. Die Spielberichte

Amerikanische Literaturszene: Ihr findet uns im Club

france24fr.title: Israël : Gadi Eisenkot invite le parti de Benjamin Netanyahu à des négociations de coalition
france24fr.description: Le centriste Gadi Eisenkot, chargé de former le prochain gouvernement israélien, a invité le parti du premier ministre sortant, Benyamin Netanyahu à des pourparlers en vue d’une éventuelle coalition, a annoncé, samedi, son parti.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle : prenant "acte de l’impasse" de sa campagne, François Ruffin retire sa candidature
france24fr.description: À cinq mois de l’échéance, François Ruffin a annoncé samedi qu’il retirait sa candidature à l’élection présidentielle, prenant "acte de l’impasse" de sa campagne faute d’avoir réussi à imposer l’organisation d’une "grande primaire" de toute la gauche.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : 82 500 personnes ont manifesté en France selon Beauvau, 150 000 d'après la CGT
Guerre en Ukraine : deux personnes tuées à Kryvyï Rih
france24fr.description: La Russie a ⁠de nouveau frappé ​dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi 21 novembre des cibles civiles dans la ville industrielle de Kryvyï Rih, ville natale du président Volodymyr Zelensky, où au moins deux personnes ont été tuées, dont un garçon de sept ans.

france24fr.title: COP31 à Antalya : bras de fer autour des énergies fossiles et des financements
france24fr.description: La 31e ⁠conférence des Nations unies sur ​les changements climatiques (COP31) aboutira soit à un accord satisfaisant, soit à aucun accord, a déclaré samedi 21 novembre le haut responsable de l'Union européenne chargé du climat, alors que les négociations se prolongeaient bien au-delà ​de l'échéance prévue. Nous en parlons avec notre correspondante Jenna Le Bras.

france24fr.title: Dakar : la Biennale des arts contemporains ouvre ses portes
france24fr.description: C'est parti pour la 16e édition de la Biennale de Dakar ! Le rendez-vous des arts contemporains a ouvert ses portes jeudi 19 novembre dans la capitale sénégalaise. Au programme de l'exposition principale, le IN : 79 artistes du continent et de ses diasporas qui explorent notamment les thèmes de la résilience et de la transformation.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : les combats se poursuivent dans le Sud-Kivu
france24fr.description: Dans l'est de la RD Congo, les combats se poursuivent dans la province du Sud-Kivu. L'armée congolaise, appuyée par les combattants wazalendo et l'armée burundaise, mène des offensives contre les Twirwaneho, alliés au Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), le mouvement politico-militaire dirigé par l'ancien président Joseph Kabila. Ces affrontements provoquent d'importants déplacements de population. Nous en parlons avec notre correspondante Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula.

france24fr.title: Guinée - Burkina Faso : pourquoi les tensions montent
france24fr.description: Les tensions montent entre la Guinée et le Burkina Faso. Conakry vient de couper le signal de la RTB, la télévision publique burkinabè. En cause : un éditorial critique, accompagné d'une caricature du président Mamadi Doumbouya. Mais l'affaire va bien au-delà de la télévision : elle éclate en pleine répression contre l'orpaillage illégal en Guinée, qui a déjà contraint des dizaines de milliers de Burkinabè à rentrer au pays.

france24fr.title: Manifestation à Paris : le cortège est arrivé à Nation "sans débordement"
france24fr.description: La mobilisation continue en France ce samedi 21 novembre. Nos journalistes Valentine Erba et Sylvain Rousseau étaient en direct du cortège parisien à son arrivée à Nation. "On peut tirer le bilan d'une journée extrêmement calme", rapporte-t-il.

france24fr.title: Climat : les négociations s'enlisent à la COP31, sans compromis en vue
france24fr.description: Certains ministres sont déjà partis, les tractations se poursuivent, mais toujours pas de terrain d'entente : la COP sur le climat traîne en longueur samedi en Turquie, où 200 pays tentent encore de trouver un accord, malgré leurs différends sur les énergies fossiles et les financements. Nous en parlons avec notre journaliste Anne Corpet.

france24fr.title: Manifestation à Paris : un cortège "finalement assez fourni"
france24fr.description: Ce samedi 21 novembre marque le sixième acte de la colère sociale en France. Des manifestations se tiennent dans de nombreuses villes à travers le pays. Notre journaliste Sylvain Rousseau suit le cortège parisien, qui est "finalement beaucoup plus fourni que ce l'on pensait au début", remarque-t-il.

france24fr.title: Verdict au procès de Michel Zecler : l'espoir d'une "jurisprudence"
france24fr.description: Dans votre magazine : les réactions après le verdict rendu hier soir en France dans le procès du passage à tabac de Michel Zecler. De la prison ferme pour les trois policiers reconnus coupables de violences aggravées, et de faux en ​écriture ‌publique. La circonstance aggravante de racisme a été retenue. Maitre Seydi Ba était notre invité.

france24fr.title: Manifestations en France : colère contre la vie chère et les violences policières
france24fr.description: Notre journaliste Sylvain Roussain est place de la République, au point de départ du cortège parisien. "Le renseignement annonce entre 15 000 et 30 000 manifestants", "ce qui n'empêche pas un dispositif policier important", rapporte-t-il. Ce sixième samedi de manifestations se tient juste après l'instauration d'une présomption d'usage légal des armes par les forces de l'ordre ce vendredi 20 novembre.

france24fr.title: Trump - Poutine : comment expliquer leur relation actuelle ?
france24fr.description: Donald Trump et Vladimir Poutine se sont rapprochés récemment, ce qui rend la position américaine assez illisible en ce qui concerne la guerre en Ukraine. Nous décryptons la situation avec notre invité Ronald Hatto, professeur de relations internationales à Sciences Po.

france24fr.title: Le baron de la drogue "El Chapo Isidro", recherché par le FB0, a été arrêté au Mexique
france24fr.description: Il était l'un des dix criminels en fuite les plus recherchés par le FBI. Le baron de la drogue "El Chapo Isidro" a été arrêté vendredi au Mexique, ont annoncé les autorités, déclenchant de violents affrontements dans l'État de Sinaloa où il opérait.

france24fr.title: Une "attaque de drone" contre un cargo russe détectée dans le golfe de Finlande
france24fr.description: Une "attaque de drone" contre un cargo russe dans le golfe de Finlande a été détectée par l'armée finlandaise, samedi, selon le ministère de la Défense du pays nordique, qui en a informé ses alliés au sein de l'Otan.

france24fr.title: Manifestations en France : la révolution en fanfare ?
france24fr.description: Au départ des récentes manifestations, il y a souvent un orchestre. La fanfare se poursuit ensuite dans le cortège : une façon d'exprimer sa colère autrement. "On peut danser une colère", assure une manifestante.

france24fr.title: Acte VI de la mobilisation : les manifestants se rassemblent place de la République
france24fr.description: Ce samedi 21 novembre, les manifestations reprennent à travers la France. Notre envoyé spécial Sylvain Rousseau est en direct de la place de la République, point de départ du cortège. "Il y a un appel à manifester dans différents pays d'Europe", rappelle-t-il.

observador.title: Samuel deu a Leonardo o que Abel já tinha dado numa bandeja
observador.description: Em São Paulo, o Flamengo de Jardim só precisava de um empate contra o Palmeiras de Abel para ser desde já bicampeão brasileiro — e foi precisamente isso que fez, com Samuel Lino a ser decisivo (1-1).

observador.title: SCP x UDS. "Penálti por marcar a favor dos leões"
observador.description: Nota 5 para Diogo Rosa, árbitro da vitória do Sporting frente ao União da Serra. Alguns erros num jogo sem VAR: golo mal validado, um penálti bem assinalado e outro por assinalar a favor dos Leões.

observador.title: 21h. Mais de 1000 ocorrências registadas até às 18h
observador.description: 1036 são os números registados pelas autoridades por todo o país, com a região de Lisboa e Vale Tejo a registar mais de 700 ocorrências.

observador.title: SCP x UDS. “Enquanto o União teve pernas…"
observador.description: Sporting "pouco esclarecido" vence equipa do quarto escalão com golos só na segunda parte. Do União da Serra, Gabriel Alves destaca David Santos, guarda-redes que adiou ao máximo o golo dos leões.

observador.title: Detido líder de cartel na lista dos mais procurados do FBI
observador.description: Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores foi detido numa mega-operação no estado de Sinaloa. A organização que liderava é acusada de transportar grandes quantidades de heroína, cocaína e fentanil para os EUA.

observador.title: "United? A análise feita até agora vai para o lixo"
observador.description: O treinador do Sporting assumiu que a equipa procurou resolver de forma individual na primeira parte, melhorando na segunda, e lembrou que mudança de treinador no United dificulta preparação do jogo.

observador.title: SCP x UDS. “Sporting cumpriu os serviços mínimos
observador.description: Para Nuno Mourão, Irankunda foi o “jogador mais” da vitória do Sporting frente ao União da Serra. Luis Guilherme foi “um a menos” e David Santos, guarda-redes do União, fez “defesas incríveis.

observador.title: Pentágono condiciona cooperação militar com Canadá
observador.description: O secretário norte-americano da Defesa impôs restrições à cooperação militar com o Canadá. Memorando do Pentágono descreve "reorientação das prioridades específicas de defesa" dos EUA.

observador.title: "Cenário mais provável é manter equilíbrio orçamental"
observador.description: Ministro das Finanças volta a atacar PS e Chega por "desvirtuarem" orçamento. Miranda Sarmento acredita que "legislatura tem todas as condições para continuar".

observador.title: Árvore de Natal e acampada partilham espaço no Porto
observador.description: Uma árvore de Natal com cerca de quatro metros de altura estava instalada na Praça D. João I, no Porto, onde desde 10 de outubro têm havido protestos e acampadas pelo direito à habitação.

observador.title: O salto mortal de quem tem uma vida inteira para viver
observador.description: O avançado australiano foi o melhor jogador da goleada do Sporting ao União da Serra e bisou para empurrar os leões para a próxima ronda da Taça, levando o salto mortal de volta a Alvalade (4-0).

observador.title: De onde vem esta sucessão "invulgar" de falhas e ataques?
observador.description: Alguns especialistas em segurança informática consideram que “é invulgar” a concentração de acontecimentos, mas descartam que estejam relacionados. IA "não explica tudo".

observador.title: Ex-Presidente do Brasil Jair Bolsonaro internado
observador.description: Jair Bolsonaro foi internado nos cuidados intensivos devido a uma obstrução intestinal parcial. O antigo Presidente está "estável" e pode ter de ser novamente submetido a uma cirurgia.

observador.title: 19h. Proteção Civil regista 700 ocorrências até às 17h
observador.description: A proteção civil indica que a região de Lisboa e Vale do Tejo registou o maior número de ocorrências, cerca de 400, mas o centro e o norte também já contaram com alguns incidentes.

observador.title: Papa alerta para riscos se tecnologia não tiver ética
observador.description: O Papa Leão XIV alertou para a necessidade de as tecnologias e as suas aplicações serem regidas segundo princípios éticos, sob pena de os riscos para a humanidade serem enormes.

observador.title: "Se PSD não quer coligação à direita, é melhor desaparecer"
observador.description: Diogo Pacheco de Amorim diz que "PSD teria lugar" num Governo do Chega, mas que, para isso, é necessário que aceite um acordo de longo prazo para "fazer reformas estruturais".

observador.title: João Reis: "O teatro é a minha fonte luminosa"
observador.description: Tenta contrariar constantemente as preocupações que tem com habitação e trabalho precário, foi marinheiro, bartender e é no teatro que se sente realizado. É o narrador de "As Sombras de Duarte Lima".

observador.title: Porsche vende mini 550 Spyder eléctrico por 83.000€
observador.description: A Porsche vai comemorar, a 21 de Novembro, 75 anos de competição. Para marcar o momento, decidiu fabricar um batalhão de 550 Spyder, o seu primeiro modelo de corridas, mas em versão mini.

nzz.title: Die Corona-Pandemie beschleunigte Altersprozesse bei Kindern, Jugendlichen und jungen Erwachsenen
nzz.description: Eine neue Studie zeigt: Die ersten zwei Lockdowns führten zu Veränderungen im Erbgut. Der Befund ist der erstmalige biologische Beweis für negative gesundheitliche Auswirkungen der Pandemie.

nzz.title: Vier Fäuste für ein Halleluja: Die Kampfansage der SVP
nzz.description: Das SVP-Ticket mit Thomas Aeschi und Michael Graber ist eine maximale Provokation. Selbst innerhalb der SVP ist von einer «Überraschung im negativen Sinn» die Rede. Man müsse unbedingt über eine wilde Wahl nachdenken, heisst es derweil aus der SP.

nzz.title: Schweizer Scharfschützenmunition: Dubioser Händler aus Slowenien verschob über eine halbe Million Patronen
nzz.description: Ein slowenischer Waffenhändler verkaufte über 500 000 Schuss aus Schweizer Produktion nach Kirgistan. Der Mann hat gegenüber den Behörden wohl falsche Angaben gemacht.

nzz.title: Kokain, Bananen und Kartelle: Die Schweiz ist Zentrum einer beispiellosen Aktion gegen den Drogenhandel
nzz.description: Es begann mit einer auffälligen Früchtelieferung – und führte zu einer internationalen Grossrazzia mit 41 Verhafteten allein in der Schweiz. Im Kampf gegen Tarnfirmen der Drogenmafias wirbt ein ranghoher Fedpol-Beamter nun für ein Bankkontenregister wie in der EU.

nzz.title: Von falschen Haaren bis zur Hand an Halle Berrys Taille: E-Mails zeigen die gnadenlose Kontrolle hinter der Marke Roger Federer
nzz.description: Interne Dokumente von Schweiz Tourismus enthüllen den extremen Perfektionismus bei der Inszenierung der Werbe-Ikone – und heikle Freundschaftsdienste der steuerfinanzierten Marketingorganisation.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Fifa-Präsidium: Auch Afrika steht hinter Infantino
nzz.description: Nach der WM im Sommer 2026 ist der Kampf um das Fifa-Präsidium entbrannt. Im März findet die Wahl des Präsidenten statt. Die jüngsten Entwicklungen und die Hintergründe im Überblick.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN KULTUR - Kunstsammler «Mick» Flick ist tot
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Feuilleton.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Neue Angriffe auf Tanker in umkämpfter Strasse von Hormuz
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Ein russischer Frachter wird im Finnischen Meerbusen von mutmasslich ukrainischen Drohnen getroffen
nzz.description: Das getroffene Schiff untersteht dem russischen Verteidigungsministerium. Ob es auch diesmal Waffen an Bord hatte, ist noch unklar. Während die Rettungsoperation läuft, verletzt ein russischer Militärhelikopter den finnischen Luftraum.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN WIRTSCHAFT - EU und Indonesien unterzeichnen weitreichenden Handelsdeal
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus der Wirtschaft.

nzz.title: Dramatische Wende 34 Jahre nach dem Mord am Mafia-Jäger Paolo Borsellino
nzz.description: Gianni De Gennaro, der frühere Polizeichef Italiens, hat sich das Leben genommen. Gegen ihn lief eine Untersuchung wegen Irreführung von Ermittlungen im Kampf gegen die Cosa Nostra.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die SVP macht Powerplay nach Drehbuch – sie weiss, sie kann sich das leisten
nzz.description: Mit Thomas Aeschi und Michael Graber nominiert die SVP zwei Hardliner für den Bundesrat. Ein ähnliches Manöver ist ihr schon einmal gelungen: mit Christoph Blocher und Ueli Maurer.

nzz.title: Mutmasslicher Drogenboss in Mexiko gefasst
nzz.description: Er steht auf der FBI-Liste der zehn meistgesuchten Flüchtigen. Mexikos Militär hat ihn nun in einem Grosseinsatz festgenommen.

nzz.title: VIDEO - So verliefen Europas Jugendproteste
nzz.description: Am Freitag gehen in mehreren europäischen Ländern junge Menschen auf die Strasse, unter anderem gegen Sparpolitik und Aufrüstung. Die Proteste bleiben grösstenteils friedlich.

nzz.title: Prozess um Palisades-Feuer in LA: Mann schuldig gesprochen
nzz.description: Anderthalb Jahre nach den Flächenbränden in Los Angeles war im Juni ein Prozess um Brandstiftung geplatzt. Die Jury konnte sich nicht einigen. Dann wurde der Fall neu aufgerollt.

nzz.title: Trump will Tech-Konzerne mit Datenzentren im Ausland hoch besteuern – und bleibt beim Ukraine-Krieg vage
nzz.description: Nach seiner Asienreise zieht Donald Trump Bilanz. Konkrete Fortschritte bei der nuklearen Abrüstung und im Ukraine-Krieg bleiben aus. Dennoch hofft er auf einen baldigen Frieden. Mit der Androhung von Strafsteuern für Tech-Konzerne sorgt er für eine Überraschung.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Deutlich weniger Teilnehmer am sechsten Protestsamstag
spiegel.description: Die Proteste gegen steigende Lebenshaltungskosten in Frankreich flachen ab. In manchen Städten kam es erneut zu Ausschreitungen.

spiegel.title: Karl Lauterbach: »Dass KI die Menschheit auslöscht, halte ich für Unsinn«
spiegel.description: Ex-Gesundheitsminister Karl Lauterbach hat gerade die wichtigsten KI-Labore in den USA und China besucht. Jetzt schlägt er Alarm: Deutschland dürfe sich nicht weiter abhängen lassen. Doch etwas macht ihm Hoffnung.

spiegel.title: António Costa kürzt, Friedrich Merz kritisiert dennoch den EU-Budget-Vorschlag
spiegel.description: Was kostet die EU-Mitgliedschaft demnächst? Ratspräsident Costa kommt dem Bundeskanzler entgegen, aber der Streit geht weiter. Steuern für Digitalkonzerne sollen die Finanzen entspannen.

spiegel.title: Polen: Flugobjekt in Polen war russische Rakete – Nato spricht von einem »gefährlichen Vorfall«
spiegel.description: Drei militärische Flugobjekte schlugen im Südosten Polens ein, laut Ministerpräsident Donald Tusk eine »Provokation« Putins. Nun schaltet sich Nato-Generalsekretär Mark Rutte ein.

spiegel.title: Finnland: Russisches Frachtschiff nach Drohnenangriff in Brand
spiegel.description: »Der Krieg greift auf Gebiete in unserer Nachbarschaft über«, so Finnlands Ministerpräsident Orpo: Vor der Küste des Landes hat vermutlich eine ukrainische Drohne ein russisches Schiff getroffen.

spiegel.title: Afghanistan: Wie brutal die Taliban die medizinische Versorgung von Frauen unterbinden
spiegel.description: Die Sittenpolizei der Taliban greift immer härter durch: Afghanische Ärzte sollen Frauen nicht einmal mehr im Notfall behandeln. Hebammen dürfen nicht mehr ausgebildet werden. Es droht eine medizinische Katastrophe.

spiegel.title: Paolo Bulgari ist tot
spiegel.description: Schon Audrey Hepburn und Elizabeth Taylor trugen Schmuck der Luxusmarke Bulgari. Nun ist Firmenchef Paolo Bulgari im Alter von 89 Jahren gestorben.

spiegel.title: Thore Schölermann über den Wechsel vom Moderator zum McDonald's-Unternehmer
spiegel.description: Tausche Millionenpublikum gegen Fast-Food-Franchise: Moderator Thore Schölermann betreibt nun drei McDonald’s-Filialen. Im Interview erklärt er den ungewöhnlichen Wechsel – und sagt, was die Jobs gemein haben.

spiegel.title: EU und Indonesien unterzeichnen weitreichenden Handelspakt
spiegel.description: Die EU gewinnt die drittgrößte Demokratie der Welt als Partner: Indonesien. Schon bald sollen dadurch etwa Zölle auf europäische Autos entfallen, das ostasiatische Land will mehr wichtige Batterierohstoffe liefern.

spiegel.title: VW, Mercedes, BMW: Wie Chinas E-Autos von der Absatzkrise in Deutschland profitieren – SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Zu hohe Arbeitskosten, Werkschließungen, Absatzkrise: Konzerne wie Volkswagen und Mercedes schwächeln, Fahrzeuge aus Chinas mischen den deutschen Automarkt auf. Unterwegs mit Gewinnern und Verlierern des Umbruchs.

spiegel.title: Tatjana Kim: Chefin von russischem Onlinehändler Wildberries tritt zurück
spiegel.description: Die Sanktionen der EU gegen die russische Unternehmerin Tatjana Kim zeigen Wirkung. Die Gründerin des »russischen Amazon« räumt ihren Führungsposten.

spiegel.title: Kaufland ruft Speisekartoffeln von Parmentine zurück
spiegel.description: Speisekartoffeln rot, festkochend: Die Handelskette Kaufland warnt vor dem Verzehr einer bestimmten Kartoffelsorte.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Christian »Mick« Flick: Spross einer Industriellendynastie ist tot
spiegel.description: Er war einer der superreichen Deutschen. Mit der skandalumwitterten Vergangenheit seiner Familie setzte er sich aktiv auseinander. Jetzt ist Friedrich Christian Flick gestorben. Er wurde 82 Jahre alt.

spiegel.title: Auswandern in die Schweiz – 12 Dinge, die Sie vorher wissen sollten
spiegel.description: Das Gehalt ist hoch, die Sprache vertraut. Doch Wohnungsmarkt, Arztrechnungen und Kitakosten überraschen viele Deutsche. Was vom Schweizer Lohn wirklich bleibt – und warum der Konjunktiv beim Ankommen hilft.

spiegel.title: Bundesliga: FC Bayern verliert Tabellenführung, Dortmund und Leipzig profitieren

phys-org.description: In April 2017, a magnitude 6.5 earthquake shook southern Africa from an unlikely place: the middle of the Kalahari Craton in eastern Botswana. Cratons are the ancient cores of continents, and this one is built from blocks of crust up to 3.7 billion years old. Geologists have long considered such regions too cold, too thick and too rigid to tear apart.

phys-org.title: From screens in class to smart glasses, Norway rethinks new technologies

phys-org.title: What makes rock deep beneath continents break away and sink?
phys-org.description: We usually picture mountain building as rock being pushed upward. But deep beneath some mountain belts and volcanic arcs, the opposite can happen: dense rock at the base of the crust can become unstable, break away and sink hundreds of kilometers into the mantle, dragging part of the rigid outer shell of the Earth (the lithosphere) with it. Seismic images suggest that this process, known as lithospheric dripping, has occurred beneath the central Andes and California's Sierra Nevada.

phys-org.title: Device that measures strawberry skin's strength will aid breeders
phys-org.description: Resilient strawberry varieties will be more easily identifiable thanks to a tool developed by University of Queensland engineering students. The prototype measures the strength of strawberry skin, a key breeding consideration for the Australian Strawberry Breeding Program at Queensland's Department of Primary Industries.

phys-org.title: Quantum software matches classical benchmark for a molecular interaction
phys-org.description: Predicting how molecules interact is central to drug discovery: it offers important information about how a new drug might work in the human body, the side effects it can cause and more. Computationally modeling these interactions can reduce the need for lengthy and expensive lab work, but some interactions still remain beyond the reach of classical computers.

phys-org.title: The call of the seamount: Two new armored tardigrades described in the Atlantic
phys-org.description: An international team led by researchers from Senckenberg am Meer in Wilhelmshaven has described two new species of marine tardigrades. The tiny marine organisms were discovered in the sediment of the Senghor Seamount off the coast of Cape Verde. According to the researchers, the discovery underscores the role of undersea mountains as oases of biodiversity. The study, which includes comprehensive taxonomic descriptions of the new species, has been published in the journal "ZooKeys."

phys-org.title: A fish as old as Montana—the blue sucker discovered to live well over 100 years
phys-org.description: Using bomb radiocarbon dating on microscopic otoliths (earstones), researchers have found that a native species of fish in the Upper Missouri River in Montana is living up to 130 years—more than triple the previous estimate of around 40 years—and some blue suckers alive today hatched in the late 1800s, around the dawn of the automobile and when Montana officially became a state.

phys-org.title: Caribbean corals are in crisis. Fossil reefs can help point to where corals may persist
phys-org.description: The fossilized remains of ancient coral reefs often sit just meters from living corals in the Caribbean, where reefs have declined sharply over the past 70 years. Those fossils could help show where corals might survive a warming future. In two new papers, researchers at The University of Texas at Austin identify which coral species dominated ancient reefs in northeastern Jamaica and suggest how that record could guide reef rehabilitation.

phys-org.title: Ancient bison hunting site in Texas challenges long-held assumptions

phys-org.title: Scientists discover twist-tunable interlayer excitons in atomically thin anisotropic semiconductors
phys-org.description: When light shines on a semiconductor, negatively charged electrons and positively charged holes—empty states left behind when electrons move away—pair up and bind together. This bound state is called an exciton. When two atomically thin semiconductor layers are stacked, electrons and holes can reside in different layers, forming what is known as an interlayer exciton (IE).

phys-org.title: Gamified mobile payment features may drive adoption among Gen-Z users

phys-org.title: Record-setting X-ray laser reliably generates flashes with wavelengths shorter than distances between atoms

proj-syn.title: Journalism Can Be More Than AI Fodder
proj-syn.description: As AI fundamentally alters the information environment, news publishers risk becoming little more than content suppliers for Big Tech. To avoid that fate, many are drawing on their archives and expertise to develop AI tools that allow them to operate and compete on their own terms.

proj-syn.title: Governing African Economies as They Are
proj-syn.description: Africa cannot overcome its development challenges by applying the same knowledge, economic, and innovation systems that helped create them. Imagining and governing new ways forward will require three intellectual ruptures.

proj-syn.title: Making Earth Cool Again
proj-syn.description: Climate multilateralism is evolving into a two-tiered system in which high-level negotiations toward shared commitments and the real-world implementation of climate solutions become more mutually supportive. Only by unleashing such virtuous cycles can we keep the 1.5ºC target for global warming within reach.

proj-syn.title: America’s Lame-Duck Autocrat
proj-syn.description: When autocrats suffer a defeat, they tend to double down, such as by intensifying repression at home or behaving more recklessly abroad. With two years left in office after historic midterm election losses, this is the road US President Donald Trump appears to be taking.

proj-syn.title: Getting Ukraine’s House in Order
proj-syn.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly opposed the idea of forming a national unity government. But bringing opposition leaders into the cabinet would ensure the checks on corruption and wayward bureaucratic action that Zelensky’s team can no longer provide.

proj-syn.title: What Adam Smith Missed
proj-syn.description: For all that he got right, the "founding father" of economics failed to see how technological innovations lead to market monopolization. If AI is left to the invisible hand, it will almost certainly increase economic and political inequality, causing even deeper social polarization and further undermining democracy.

proj-syn.title: China Ratchets Up Its Weaponization of Trade
proj-syn.description: Just as the US has been leveraging its large market and technological leadership for geopolitical ends, China is now using its dominance in critical minerals, industrial inputs, and specialized manufacturing machinery to coerce and punish other countries. The consequences, both economic and geopolitical, are far-reaching.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Thing to Talk About With Russia
proj-syn.description: The European security order’s foundational principle is never to tolerate aggression. There is no need to revise that order, as the Kremlin has proposed, only to wait for a Russian regime that is willing to respect other countries’ territorial integrity and uphold its own previous commitments.

proj-syn.title: The Truth About Global AI Governance
proj-syn.description: Because the current approach to global AI governance presumes that developing countries are full of eager adopters of AI who need to be cautioned about the technology's risks, it overlooks what their information environments and media markets actually need. A survey of researchers who study 71 countries sets the record straight.

proj-syn.title: Demography is the Achilles’ Heel of Dictatorships
proj-syn.description: Governments that manipulate population figures often end up deceiving themselves as much as the public. When autocratic leaders mistake inflated numbers for real national strength, they make costly strategic mistakes and fail to address their countries’ demographic decline until it is too late.

proj-syn.title: The Silver Lining of a Data-Center Slowdown
proj-syn.description: With leading AI labs under intense competitive pressure to keep advancing the frontier of the technology's capabilities, resistance to the build-out of computing resources is not such a bad thing. The more time we can buy, the greater our chances of maximizing the potential benefits and mitigating the risks.

proj-syn.title: What Nvidia’s Crisis Reveals About the Chip War
proj-syn.description: Export restrictions, like those depriving China of Nvidia’s most advanced chips, may buy time by curtailing a competitor's access to frontier capabilities made elsewhere. But in any technological conflict, policymakers must remember that slowing a rival is not the same as strengthening oneself.

proj-syn.title: When Export Restraints Are the Lesser Evil
proj-syn.description: Governments face pressure to protect domestic industries while preserving access to cheaper foreign goods. The recent EU-China car-export deal offers an uneasy compromise that protects European automakers while keeping Chinese cars available to consumers, making it preferable to prohibitive tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Trade Losses That Nobody Counts
proj-syn.description: While much of the United Kingdom’s post-Brexit debate has focused on the monetary value of lost trade with the European Union, the composition of UK-EU trade flows warrants closer attention. A sharp decline in the variety of products shipped to Europe suggests that the economic costs have been greater than many realize.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Big Bet on Health Care
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s dependence on imported medicines and medical equipment leaves families exposed to exchange-rate fluctuations and hospitals at the mercy of global supply chains. Expanding domestic manufacturing is essential to reducing the cost of treatment and ensuring that more Nigerians can access quality care.

proj-syn.title: What Should the Nvidia Board Do?
proj-syn.description: The proper role of any corporate board is to strike a careful balance between stakeholders. In Nvidia's case, the board will have to consider not just the current trading price, but also how its decisions will affect the landscape in which it operates, its employees, and its license to trade.

proj-syn.title: The Roots of Macron’s Failure
proj-syn.description: Although French President Emmanuel Macron has certainly made mistakes, his troubled presidency is symptomatic of a deeper problem. In the end, he failed to build something truly enduring because he was seduced by the same monarchical impulse that is a recurring feature of French political culture.

proj-syn.title: Yalta in Shenzhen?
proj-syn.description: In principle, the planned summit of the US, Russian, and Chinese presidents could usefully address what should be done to limit the proliferation of nuclear weapons, ensure that AI is more a force for good than harm, and end ongoing wars and prevent new ones. But principle is one thing; in practice, we are likely to see something else.

crunchbase.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Reflecting Sunlight From Space, Better Breathing And Smarter Garbage Trucks
crunchbase.description: What if solar farms could keep generating electricity after sunset with a little help from mirrors orbiting Earth? Or researchers could send an experiment into space for less than the price of a car? Our latest roundup also includes a company bringing AI to the old-school business of garbage hauling, another rethinking how factories are programmed, and a consumer brand betting that better breathing could become a big business.

crunchbase.title: What The Telecom Bust Taught Me About AI’s Debt Boom
crunchbase.description: The AI buildout’s growing reliance on debt echoes the telecom bubble, raising the risk that infrastructure spending will outpace the revenue needed to meet fixed repayment obligations. According to guest author David Spreng of Runway Growth Capital, even if AI fulfills its technological promise, borrowers’ survival will depend on realistic demand forecasts and debt tied to dependable cash flows, with missed timelines potentially forcing restructurings and bankruptcies.

crunchbase.title: The Blue Economy: The World’s Quietest Economic Engine And Its Smartest Cities
crunchbase.description: The $2.6 trillion blue economy is creating startup opportunities in maritime automation, clean energy and logistics, with blue tech funding nearing $10 billion through Q3 2026, driven largely by major defense deals. Alberto Onetti, chairman of Mind the Bridge, writes that ports are emerging as hubs for testing and scaling these technologies, but realizing their potential requires coordination among port authorities, startups, investors and policymakers.

crunchbase.title: What’s Next For Recruiting, Job Hunting And HR? More AI, Of Course
crunchbase.description: So far this year, venture backers have poured close to $4 billion into an assortment of global companies focused on recruiting, finding jobs and streamlining processes associated with HR and payroll management, Crunchbase data shows. Not surprisingly, the vast majority are also incorporating a heavy dose of AI.

crunchbase.title: Public Markets Are Frequently Wrong. The SaaSpocalypse Shows Us Why
crunchbase.description: The “SaaSpocalypse” selloff and uneven recovery exposed public markets’ difficulty distinguishing software companies that benefit from AI from those it threatens, particularly as deeply embedded platforms retain competitive advantages. In this guest essay, Richard Anton, co-founder and general partner of Oxx, argues that this volatility distorts private transaction pricing, undermines confidence in public ownership and makes IPOs less appealing to founders.

crunchbase.title: Anthropic Closes Up 17% After Massive IPO
crunchbase.description: The offering promises to be the public market event of the season, with the Claude creator seeing investor demand for shares well in excess of its capital-raising goals.

crunchbase.title: The Key Numbers I’m Watching As Anthropic Makes Its IPO Debut
crunchbase.description: Just three years after launching with zero revenue, Anthropic brought in $17 billion and says more than 11,900 customers now spend at least $100,000 a year. But its IPO filing also reveals enormous computing commitments and big questions about balancing growth with risks.

crunchbase.title: What To Measure When ARR Isn’t Enough
crunchbase.description: AI companies’ hybrid subscription, usage and outcome-based pricing makes headline ARR figures an unreliable measure of predictable revenue, often obscuring differences in customer commitments and spending patterns. Guest author Kenza Zayani, an early-stage investor at RTP Global, warns that as these businesses seek growth capital, investors increasingly expect evidence of retention, expansion, revenue predictability and sustainable margins to assess the durability of growth.
